archetypes.name: kv-parser-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a two-KV grammar emitted by four launchers and parsed by ship-pr.sh; cross-file token consistency and the safe-default parse path are high-risk plan surfaces not covered by the static arch/edge panels.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the new LAUNCHER_FAILURE_CLASS and LAUNCHER_FAILURE_REASON KV token sets are enumerated identically across lib-external-launcher-common.sh, all three CI launchers, the ship-pr.sh guard, and the sibling .md contract files the plan lists. Check whether the plan specifies the parse logic (awk pattern, field delimiter, variable name) used in ship-pr.sh's run_ci_fix_vendor guard, and whether the safe-default behavior described in Edge case #2 (unrecognized class defaults to health) is precisely enough specified for an implementer to get it right without re-reading the rationale section. Verify that the 'none' class emitted on LAUNCHER_EXIT=0 is explicitly handled in the ship-pr.sh guard so a successful cursor run cannot inadvertently trigger the bail path. Check whether the test cases pinning the token literals are specified precisely enough that a future token rename would cause a structural test failure rather than a silent behavior change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: dep-sequencing
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts a hard BLOCKED_BY on issue #2669 to avoid conflating diagnostic states while simultaneously claiming forward-compatibility; this apparent contradiction may represent a plan decision that is either over-conservative or internally inconsistent.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the plan's claim that issue #2669 must land first to avoid conflating 'first-fixer-non-health' with whatever taxonomy #2669 settles, and check whether the plan shows a concrete user-visible defect (wrong exit path, wrong BAIL_REASON token, wrong diagnostic) that would occur if this plan ships without #2669. If the forward-compat claim ('reuses exit 3 with a new BAIL_REASON token, forward-compatible with #2669') is accurate, verify that the plan does not simultaneously treat the dependency as strictly blocking, since those two claims are in tension. Check whether the new BAIL_REASON token 'first-fixer-non-health' would collide with or be shadowed by any exit-3 taxonomy #2669 might introduce after the fact. Identify whether the plan provides a rollback or migration path if #2669 lands after this issue and restructures the exit-3 BAIL_REASON namespace. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sentinel-write-order
archetypes.rationale: The infinite-loop guardrail depends on a fail-closed sentinel-write-before-attempt ordering that the plan names as a critical invariant in Failure mode #2, but the Step 8+ control flow description does not clearly constrain the write order or FAILED_RUN_ID sourcing.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the skills/implement/SKILL.md Step 8+ control flow description in the plan and verify it explicitly specifies that the sentinel file write and counter increment occur strictly before the main-agent CI fix attempt begins, not after. Check whether the plan identifies the exact source of FAILED_RUN_ID (which ship-pr-state.sh key, set by which script, at which phase) so the sentinel path is deterministic and cannot collide across separate /implement invocations that reuse the same IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR. Verify that the plan describes the counter initialization, increment, and read idiom consistently, and whether the cap of 3 is inclusive or exclusive of the triggering attempt. Check whether the plan addresses what happens if the sentinel write itself fails (e.g., IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR not yet created) and whether that failure is treated as a bail or a skip. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
